source_quote: Upon UV irradiation at 2.5 and 3.5 mJ/cm2, the E. coli viability decreased to 5.6 x 10-2 and 2.0 x 10-2, respectively (Conditions 1 and 2 in Fig. 4b; Supplemental material 5).
notes: 262 nm UV-LED, 32 mm above a stirred 15 mL suspension of E. coli K-12 (10^5-10^6 CFU/mL) in PBS; cells grown in LB to OD600 0.3-0.5 before dilution. PREPRINT (bioRxiv), not peer reviewed.

source_quote: Upon UV irradiation at 2.5 and 3.5 mJ/cm2, the E. coli viability decreased to 5.6 x 10-2 and 2.0 x 10-2, respectively (Conditions 1 and 2 in Fig. 4b; Supplemental material 5).
notes: 262 nm UV-LED, 32 mm above a stirred 15 mL suspension of E. coli K-12 (10^5-10^6 CFU/mL) in PBS; cells grown in LB to OD600 0.3-0.5 before dilution. PREPRINT (bioRxiv), not peer reviewed.

source_quote: In contrast, single-dose irradiation with 6.0 mJ/cm2 resulted in a significantly lower viability of 5.0 x 10-4 (Condition 4 in Fig. 4c).
notes: 262 nm UV-LED, 32 mm above a stirred 15 mL suspension of E. coli K-12 (10^5-10^6 CFU/mL) in PBS; cells grown in LB to OD600 0.3-0.5 before dilution. PREPRINT (bioRxiv), not peer reviewed. Single-dose exposure.

source_quote: As mentioned above, when sequential irradiation (2.5 followed by 3.5 mJ/cm2) was applied, the total fluence amounted to 6.0 mJ/cm2, yielding a viability of 5.4 x 10-3 (Condition 3 in Fig. 4b).
notes: 262 nm UV-LED, 32 mm above a stirred 15 mL suspension of E. coli K-12 (10^5-10^6 CFU/mL) in PBS; cells grown in LB to OD600 0.3-0.5 before dilution. PREPRINT (bioRxiv), not peer reviewed. SEQUENTIAL exposure: 2.5 mJ/cm2, then 30 min dark incubation at room temperature, then 3.5 mJ/cm2 (total 6.0 mJ/cm2). ~10x higher viability than a single 6.0 mJ/cm2 dose (record ecoli-uv-40462972-03); do not treat as an equivalent single-dose point.
